title: Ordinary Kunneth for a general morphism
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of
separated finite-type
schemes, let $Z$ be an auxiliary such scheme, and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ in the
finite-Tor constructible
category. Then the canonical comparison

$$
Rf_*L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} Q
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R(f\times\operatorname{id}_Z)_*\bigl(L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L} Q\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $L$ and $Q$.

external.place: (*Provenance:* Stacks Project, Étale Cohomology, Lemma 59.97.8, [Tag `0F1N`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1N), which is [lem-kun-0f1n] here, together with SGA 5, III, 1.1 and 1.6.4 for the coefficient and site generality used here.)

proof.text: Work over the fixed field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]; all products are over $k$, and all scheme morphisms are $k$-morphisms. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is finite local with $\varpi_E^n=0$ and residue field $\kappa=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)$ finite. Its characteristic is $\ell$: $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell$ belongs to the maximal ideal. Thus $\mathbf F_\ell\hookrightarrow\kappa$ is an extension of finite fields and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. The morphism $f$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], applied to $X\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target]. The same two statements apply to $h=f\times\operatorname{id}_Z:X\times_kZ\to Y\times_kZ$. The products are separated finite-type $k$-schemes: on product affine charts their algebras are generated by the two finite lists of generators, and their diagonals are products of the two closed diagonals, using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Hence $f,h$ are quasi-compact and, by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], quasi-separated. These are the geometric hypotheses needed for coefficient and site comparisons below.

source.place: Opening product diagram and coefficient datum; hypotheses for Steps 1–2

proof.text: First prove the formula on the small étale sites. For the pro-étale inputs in the statement, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies bounded constructible étale objects $L_e,Q_e$ and isomorphisms $L\simeq\nu_X^*L_e$, $Q\simeq\nu_Z^*Q_e$. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii), both étale objects have finite Tor amplitude. Write them temporarily as $L,Q$. Choose a bounded flat $A$-model $P$ of $L$ by the étale clause of [lem-sf-flat-model]. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], this bounded flat model is K-flat. No projectivity of its terms is required. The eventual transport back to the pro-étale site is carried out in the last step.

source.place: Step 2: bounded flat model; final site transport in the unit proof

proof.text:
Put $p_X:X\times Z\to X$, $p_Z:X\times Z\to Z$, $p_Y:Y\times Z\to Y$, $p'_Z:Y\times Z\to Z$, and $h=f\times\operatorname{id}_Z$. For any constant coefficient ring $R$ write $\alpha_R(L,Q)$ for the composite
$$p_Y^*Rf_*L\otimes_R^Lp_Z'^*Q\longrightarrow Rh_*p_X^*L\otimes_R^Lp_Z'^*Q\longrightarrow Rh_*(p_X^*L\otimes_R^Lp_Z^*Q).$$
The first arrow is [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] tensored with $p_Z'^*Q$ and the second is [def-kun-projection-formula-map]; $p_Z=p'_Z h$. By those mate definitions and [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], its $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ transpose is precisely the tensor of $p_X^*(f^*Rf_*L\to L)$ with $1_{p_Z^*Q}$, after the Cartesian inverse-image identification and tensor symmetry. This explicit transpose will identify all comparisons below. The external products in the conclusion mean this pullback–tensor expression, as in [def-trf-external-product], extended to the ambient derived categories by the same formula. In particular no claim that the separate exchange and projection arrows are always invertible is used.

source.place: Opening paragraph: definition of the canonical comparison

proof.text: For $R=\mathbf F_\ell$, specialize [lem-kun-0f1n] with its diagram $X\leftarrow X'\leftarrow Y$ equal to $Z\leftarrow Z\times_kY\leftarrow Z\times_kX$, and $S'\leftarrow T$ equal to $Y\xleftarrow fX$. Set its $E=Q$, $F=L$ and its integer $n=\ell$. All its schemes are finite type over the field $k$ and $\ell$ is invertible there. Its canonical arrow, after interchanging the two tensor factors and the two product coordinates, is $\alpha_{\mathbf F_\ell}(L,Q)$: its adjunct is exactly the tensor of the counit and the identity specified in the preceding step. Thus this arrow is invertible for arbitrary derived $\mathbf F_\ell$-complexes; in particular for all the bounded-below complexes used here.

Now let $B$ be any finite extension of $F=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $U,V$ be bounded-below $B$-complexes for which the indicated tensors are bounded below (in the application $V$ is bounded). Restrict coefficients to $F$. The canonical inverse-/direct-image comparisons of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] identify inverse images and $Rf_*,Rh_*$ before and after restriction. Their unit/counit compatibilities are [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities]. The $F$-arrow of the preceding step is $B\otimes_F B$-linear: naturality for multiplication by $b$ on $U$, and independently by $c$ on $V$, gives the two commuting coefficient actions. Apply the idempotent $e\in B\otimes_F B$ of [lem-pur-finite-field-derived-tensor-summand]. That node identifies the source $e$-summand with the restriction of $p_Y^*Rf_{*,B}U\otimes_B^Lp_Z'^*V$, and the inner target $e$-summand with the restriction of $p_X^*U\otimes_B^Lp_Z^*V$. Additive derived direct image preserves this splitting: apply it to the inclusion and retraction, whose composite is the identity, and to their complementary idempotents. The balanced tensor map sends the $F$-linear adjunct of step 3 to the $B$-linear tensor of the counit with the identity; the cited counit compatibility shows that the induced summand arrow is $\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B(U,V)$ itself. An invertible map commuting with $e$ induces an invertible map on its image (restrict its inverse). Restriction of scalars is conservative, since it leaves underlying cohomology groups unchanged. Hence $\alpha_B(U,V)$ is invertible. Apply this with $B=\kappa$. Finite freeness alone is not being used as a substitute for the idempotent.

source.place: Step 2: finite-field coefficient comparison, explicit diagonal summand argument

proof.text: For fixed $L$, consider the two functors in $Q$ on the bounded-below étale derived category, with values in the ambient unbounded derived category, given by the source and target of $\alpha_A$. The source tensor need not a priori be bounded below; the target tensor is bounded below because it is computed with the bounded flat model $p_X^*P$. They are exact triangulated functors: inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and induces a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; derived tensor is triangulated by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated]; bounded-below derived direct image is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. For the direct image, apply its bounded-below triangulated statement to those target tensors, then include its values in the ambient derived category. The natural transformation in step 3 respects these triangles: the counit and tensor maps commute with shifts; on a cone $\operatorname{Cone}(u)=Q_2\oplus Q_1[1]$, tensoring uses the total differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes dy$. The diagonal blocks are the maps for $Q_2,Q_1[1]$ and the off-diagonal block commutes by naturality for $u$. Thus the resulting three maps form a morphism of triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], its isomorphism locus is closed under distinguished triangles and shifts. The successive truncation triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] therefore reduce a bounded $Q$ to its finitely many cohomology sheaves $H^j(Q)[-j]$. For a single sheaf $M$, the finite filtration $M\supset\varpi_E M\supset\cdots\supset\varpi_E^nM=0$ has successive quotients $M_i=\varpi_E^iM/\varpi_E^{i+1}M$ annihilated by $\varpi_E$, hence sheaves of $\kappa$-modules. The short exact sequences $0\to\varpi_E^{i+1}M\to\varpi_E^iM\to M_i\to0$ give distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Starting at the zero sheaf and descending from $i=n-1$ to $0$, it suffices to prove $\alpha_A(L,M_i)$ invertible. No finite-Tor assumption on the individual $M_i$ is needed.

source.place: Step 2: exactness in Q and finite uniformizer filtration

proof.text:
Let $M$ be any degree-zero $\kappa$-module sheaf on $Z$. Put $L_\kappa=L\otimes_A^L\kappa$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P\otimes_A\kappa$ computes $L_\kappa$ as a bounded flat $\kappa$-complex. Use [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] with the finite $A$-algebra $B=\kappa$ to identify $(Rf_{*,A}L)\otimes_A^L\kappa$ with $Rf_{*,\kappa}L_\kappa$ by its specified counit-defined isomorphism. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is separated finite type and $L$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. For any $A$-complex $H$, a K-flat flat-term resolution $P_H$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], followed by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], computes the canonical identity
$$H\otimes_A^L\operatorname{Res}M\simeq\operatorname{Res}((H\otimes_A^L\kappa)\otimes_\kappa^LM).$$
Indeed the termwise balanced isomorphism sends $x\otimes m$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes m$, with inverse $(x\otimes a)\otimes m\mapsto x\otimes am$; these mutually inverse maps are sheaf maps, commute with differentials and extend to total tensors. To justify computing with the unresolved sheaf $M$, choose a K-flat resolution $T\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The cone is acyclic, so [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $P_H\otimes_A\operatorname{Cone}(T\to M)$ acyclic. Hence $P_H\otimes_A T\to P_H\otimes_A M$ is a quasi-isomorphism; [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies its source with the derived tensor. The identical argument over $\kappa$, using the K-flat flat-term complex $P_H\otimes_A\kappa$ supplied by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], computes the right-hand side with $M$. Pullback commutes with the coefficient tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the two factorizations of the same ringed-topos pullback; alternatively these same pure-tensor maps on pulled-back K-flat models give the identification. Apply this first to $H=p_Y^*Rf_*L$, then to $H=p_X^*L$. Together with the coefficient direct-image isomorphism and [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] for $h$, it identifies the two sides of $\alpha_A(L,M)$ with the restrictions of the two sides of $\alpha_\kappa(L_\kappa,M)$. The arrow is also identified: transpose under $h^*\dashv Rh_*$, use the counit normalization of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] and [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities], and both composites are the balanced tensor of the $\kappa$-counit with $1_M$, by step 3. Thus it is invertible by step 5. Step 6 now proves the étale assertion for the original bounded $Q$.

source.place: Step 2: coefficient transport to A; missing direct-image coefficient comparison made explicit

proof.text:
Return to $L\simeq
u_X^*L_e$, $Q\simeq
u_Z^*Q_e$ from step 2. Apply the exact comparison pullback of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] to the étale isomorphism. The pullback comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for $
u$, identify external products with pro-étale external products. The specified direct-image comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] for $f$ and $h$ identify their derived direct images; these maps are invertible because $f,h$ are qcqs and all the complexes input to direct image are bounded below (use the bounded flat models). They identify the arrow as well: its transpose from step 3 contains only inverse-image composition, tensor, and the counit of $f$; the comparison-pullback node respects composition and Cartesian identifications, while the displayed counit-normalization identity of the direct-image canonical-mate node sends the étale counit to the pro-étale counit. Hence the transported transpose is exactly the pro-étale transpose, so uniqueness in the adjunction gives the required canonical comparison. Every original comparison is natural in $L,Q$, by its counit construction; inverses of the proved natural isomorphism are natural as well. This proves the item with its pro-étale coefficient conventions, and also proves its étale reading.

source.place: Final naturality paragraph and unit sentence: comparison transports to the pro-étale site

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q55-c1963d065 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and wrote review.md; no fix files. Shape: one commit, three files (item, unit realized/realized_by, report), no new nodes. The item statement is word for word the same as in main-20261015 and the master snapshot. All 35 cited nodes exist and are unmerged, the dependency closure has no cycle, and no existing node duplicates this f×id Künneth. No SGA source is used. Source check: I compared Stacks 0F1N (etale-cohomology.tex l.20878-20937) with the step 4 substitution: X:=Z, S':=Y, X':=Z×Y, T:=X, g:=f, so p=p'_Z, f'=p_Y, h=id×f, e=p_X, with n=ℓ invertible in k. This gives α_{F_ℓ} up to symmetry, for unbounded complexes. Steps: (1) coefficient conventions give ℓ≠p and A=O_E/ϖ^n local with residue field κ of characteristic ℓ; f and h are separated, finite type and qcqs. (2) constructible-origin(ii) and comparison-tor-amplitude(ii) give étale representatives (bounded below, as required); flat-model gives a bounded flat P, which is K-flat. (3) α is exchange then PF_h, the blueprint's arrow, and its transpose is p_X*ε_f⊗1. (5) the separability idempotent from finite-field-derived-tensor-summand, restriction comparisons on D⁺ (valid because tensors over a field are underived) and conservativity of restriction pass from F_ℓ to κ. (6) the triangulated dévissage uses the finite ϖ-filtration; no Tor condition is put on the quotients. (7) lem-coef-finite-direct-image with B=κ gives Rf_*L⊗κ≅Rf_{*,κ}L_κ with counit normalisation. This fills a gap the blueprint passes over silently; the balanced identity is proved from K-flat resolutions. (8) comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate (qcqs maps, D⁺ inputs) and the pullback comparisons carry the named arrow to the pro-étale site. The coefficient category is pro-étale D^b_ctf(A_{E,n}) throughout, with no silent identification of categories. Edge cases: f=id, empty or zero inputs, n=1, A=Z/ℓ², [κ:F_ℓ] divisible by ℓ, Z=Spec k. I accept the declared off-route tools (sbc restriction comparisons, finite-field tensor summand, coef-finite-direct-image, pbc triangulated/K-flat/site-comparison nodes, change of rings) as generic black boxes; the extra declarations of route nodes are harmless. Minor: the report lists citations.json, which is not among the committed files.
